task: N7.1 — Outbox Pattern — Auditoría y preflight

databaseTransactionSurface.appDbContext: EF Core persistence boundary; SaveChangesAsync is the central durable write path.
databaseTransactionSurface.unitOfWork: Explicit BeginTransaction/Commit/Rollback with full-operation retry for MySQL 1205/1213; nested operations reuse an existing transaction.

criticalExternalEffects.currentBehavior: FacturaCompartirService generates the PDF and calls IEmailService/SmtpEmailService directly; delivery history/audit is persisted only after the SMTP call returns.
criticalExternalEffects.idempotency: Optional Idempotency-Key is protected only by process-local ConcurrentDictionary/Semaphore cache and is not durable across restart or multiple instances.

criticalExternalEffects.flow: Cloudinary product image upload/delete and server-side download
criticalExternalEffects.currentBehavior: External Cloudinary/HTTP calls are direct after server-side tenant validation.

problemStatement: A successful external send can occur before durable local history/audit, leaving sent-but-not-recorded state if the process fails after SMTP accepts the message.
A committed business mutation can lose a corresponding external effect if the process fails before the provider call when future flows couple state changes and notification.
Process-memory idempotency cannot prevent duplicate sends after restart or across multiple instances.
Retries without durable event identity can create duplicate external effects or ambiguous delivery state.

in: Define durable OutboxMessage/event contract and lifecycle.
Persist outbox intent in the same database transaction as the business state that requires the external side effect.
Use server-side tenant identity and immutable event/idempotency identity.
Define dispatcher claim/concurrency, retry/backoff, attempts, timestamps, last-error and dead-letter behavior.
Integrate invoice email as the first concrete external-effect candidate without changing public API semantics unnecessarily.
Classify storage-provider operations separately and keep binary payloads out of the outbox.
out: No large implementation in N7.1.A PRE.
No schema migration in PRE; migration belongs to DB_MIG microtask.
No secrets/provider credentials in outbox payloads.

minimumFields: PayloadJson containing only necessary non-secret metadata
Concurrency token or atomic claim marker
dispatcher: Atomically claim work so concurrent instances cannot deliver the same row simultaneously.
Retry transient failures with bounded backoff; terminal failures become observable DeadLetter/Failed state.
Provider request must use stable event/idempotency identity where supported.
Never expose cross-tenant rows or accept tenant identity from untrusted client payload.

acceptanceCriteria: A required external side effect has a durable intent recorded in the same transaction as its triggering business state before dispatch.
Rollback of the business transaction leaves no dispatchable outbox item.
Committed intent is eventually dispatchable after restart.
Retries and concurrent workers do not produce duplicate delivery for one durable event identity within the application's controllable boundary.
Tenant isolation is server-side and fail-closed.
Poison events are bounded, observable and recoverable without blocking unrelated events.
No secrets or binary document/image bodies are persisted in generic outbox payloads.
Existing invoice email API keeps deterministic error semantics while moving durability/idempotency from memory to persistent state.
directedTestPlan: business rollback => zero dispatchable outbox rows
commit => one durable pending row and eventual delivery
process restart between commit and send => eventual delivery without losing intent
process restart after provider success but before local finalization => stable idempotency/reconciliation behavior
two dispatcher instances => one successful claim/delivery per event
permanent/poison failure => Failed/DeadLetter with sanitized error
tenant A cannot read/claim tenant B records through tenant-facing surfaces
invoice email Idempotency-Key maps to durable identity instead of process-local cache
rollbackStrategy: Keep later schema changes additive while rollout is incomplete.
Dispatcher can be disabled without deleting pending rows.
If later migration fails before activation, rollback schema according to DB_MIG evidence.
Once outbox is active, rollback must preserve pending/delivered audit records and avoid re-enabling direct dual-write paths without an explicit compatibility plan.
